brief: NVIDIA's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO and a director effective immediately. Harvey Jones stays Chairman while the board's internal investigation into Huang's conduct continues. The board says it received assurance from senior US government levels that reinstatement poses no national security risk, and a Trump social-media post said the government has no evidence of unlawful conduct by Huang. Bernstein downgraded NVDA to Market Perform and halved its target 11 days ago on expectation Huang would be removed, which happened the next day. The stock then fell almost 30% to close near $125 Friday. With Huang back and Bernstein still positive on AI buildout fundamentals, it upgrades NVDA back to Outperform today and holds its $200 target, about 10x CY28/29 average EPS, which it says still reflects meaningful downside. Bernstein says the episode exposed board governance weakness, questions whether concessions, possibly China-related, were required given continuing political scrutiny as Democrats gain power, and says Huang's willingness to lie to the board is troubling. It also notes investor concern over AI spending sustainability predates and extends beyond Huang's removal.
